extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting software papers to the Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS) / Open Journals
extracted.subtask_description: Formatting and content requirements for submitting a short software-focused paper to JOSS/Open Journals, including required sections, metadata, length limits, and compilation checks. Targets authors of research software preparing a Markdown manuscript and accompanying repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Markdown with YAML metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted articles must use Markdown and must provide a metadata section at the beginning of the article. Format metadata using YAML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The information provided in the YAML metadata is included in the title and sidebar of the generated PDF. Provide the limited set of metadata shown in examples (authors, affiliations, date, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper length
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper should be between 750–1750 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors submitting papers significantly longer than 1750 words may be asked to reduce the length. JOSS papers are not 'full length' articles and should not contain extended software documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary (required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin your paper with a summary of the high-level functionality of your software for a non-specialist reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid jargon in this section. Explain software functionality and domain of use to a diverse, non-specialist audience. This section should be at the start of the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of need (required)
rubrics_metrics.description: A section that clearly illustrates the research purpose of the software and places it in the context of related work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state what problems the software is designed to solve, who the target audience is, and its relation to other work.

rubrics_metrics.name: State of the field (required)
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of how this software compares to other commonly-used packages in the research area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If related tools exist, provide a clear 'build vs. contribute' justification explaining your unique scholarly contribution and why existing alternatives are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software design (required)
rubrics_metrics.description: An explanation of the trade-offs you weighed, the design/architecture you chose, and why it matters for your research application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate meaningful design thinking beyond a superficial code-structure description; explain architectural decisions and their research relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research impact statement (required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of realized impact (publications, external use, integrations) or credible near-term significance (benchmarks, reproducible materials, community-readiness signals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence should be compelling and specific, not aspirational. Mention representative past or ongoing research projects and recent scholarly publications enabled by the software (if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: AI usage disclosure (required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparent disclosure of any use of generative AI in the software creation, documentation, or paper authoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no AI tools were used, state this explicitly. If AI tools were used, describe how they were used and how the quality and correctness of AI-generated content was verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors and affiliations (required formatting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a list of the authors of the software and their affiliations, using the correct format in metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiliations require an index and name. Optionally annotate the top-level organization with an ROR identifier using the 'ror' key. Name parts (given-names, surname, particles, suffix) may be used to ensure correct display; a literal display name can be provided as a last resort.

rubrics_metrics.name: References and bibliography
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of key references, including to other software addressing related needs. Bibliographic data should be collected in a paper.bib file in BibLaTeX (or plain BibTeX) format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References should include full names of venues (journals/conferences), not discipline-specific abbreviations. Cite entries by identifier (e.g., [@upper1974]); see pandoc manual for page locators, prefixes, suffixes, and suppression of author names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgements
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge any financial support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include acknowledgements as a section where relevant; explicitly mention funding sources and other support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: don't include API documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Software documentation such as API functionality should not be included in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: API or detailed documentation belongs in the software's documentation; the paper should focus on high-level functionality, design, impact, and scholarly context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper metadata details: date format
rubrics_metrics.description: The date must be specified using the format '%e %B %Y' (e.g., '9 October 2024').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the date in the YAML metadata under the 'date' key using the specified format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal cross-references support
rubrics_metrics.description: Open Journals supports a limited set of LaTeX commands for internal references: \label, \ref, and \autoref.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements that were marked with \label can be referenced with \ref and \autoref. Use labels in captions for tables/figures and either label equations directly or add a Markdown span with a label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and figures labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables and figures can be referenced if they are given a label in the caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In pure Markdown, add an empty span []{label="floatlabel"} to the caption, or use LaTeX \label{floatlabel}. Link to floats with \ref{identifier} or \autoref{identifier}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure syntax and captions
rubrics_metrics.description: To create a figure, a captioned image must appear by itself in a paragraph with the figure syntax '![caption](path)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The figure syntax must be the only element in the paragraph (surrounded by blank lines) to be treated as a figure rather than an inline image. Images larger than the text area are scaled to fit; you can specify height/width attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equations and math formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark math with $ for inline math and $$ for display math; use TeX syntax for formulae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For equations that need referencing, include a \label in the equation or use a Markdown span to add the label: [$$...$$]{label="eq:label"}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grid tables for complex tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Grid tables allow spanning columns, footers, intra-cell body elements, multi-row headers, and multi-row cells using characters '-', '=', '|', '+'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use colons in separator lines to control alignment; equals signs create headers/footers. Examples provided for layout conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markdown: semantic inline markup
rubrics_metrics.description: Inline markup in Markdown should be semantic, not presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use emphasis, strong emphasis, code spans, sub/superscript, and other semantic constructs rather than ad-hoc presentation markup. Examples of markup and rendered output are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax for footnotes uses the caret character '^'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnote identifiers need not be sequential and can be any sequence of characters without whitespace (e.g., [^marker]); numbers will be reordered automatically in the published output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings usage limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Start headings at the first level (#). The maximum supported level is 5; authors are encouraged to limit to the first two or three levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fourth- and fifth-level subsections are supported but discouraged; use lists instead of deep heading nesting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lists and enumerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use bullet lists and numbered lists to present sequential and hierarchical information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerations start with the number of the first item; examples show formatting and inclusion of math in list items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing: article and software
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are published under a Creative Commons license and software should use an OSI-approved license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include license information appropriately (e.g., footnote stating articles are under CC). Ensure software repository includes an OSI-approved license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compilation checks (must verify paper builds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should check that their paper compiles to PDF using the Open Journals toolchain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include: using the Open Journals GitHub Action (provides PDF artifact), using the provided Docker image to compile locally, or cloning the inara repository and running the inara script after installing dependencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label placement for floats and equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Labels for floats must appear in captions; equation labels can be included directly in the formula or via a Markdown span.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referencing behavior: \ref yields float number, \autoref inserts the type and number. Provide labels consistently for consistent referencing throughout the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage hyperlinks but require formal citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Open Journal publications encourage hyperlinks to websites and external resources but standard scientific practice of citing relevant publications must be followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hyperlinks for external resources for convenience, but still include formal bibliographic citations for scholarly works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid typesetting/publishing pitfalls: accessibility and PDF tagging
rubrics_metrics.description: The publishing pipeline aims to produce tagged PDF/A-3 for accessibility; decisions (e.g., use of ConTeXt vs. LaTeX) are made to support tagging requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should follow structural and semantic markup (headings, figures, tables, alt text) to facilitate accessible output; avoid hacks that break PDF tagging.
